vectors.name: folder/layout-one-new-file-per-write
vectors.description: A folder with a slot, two wraps for one person and epoch (names differ), and one new file per written record. Alice's chain: genesis (seq 1) and the member record (seq 2) are each alone in a .mseg; her content records at seq 3, 4 and 5 are one .seg each; bob has his own directory. No file is ever changed (8.1 draft 3), and the names are <first seq>-<last seq> in ten digits.

vectors.name: folder/overlapping-segments
vectors.description: Two segments of alice's chain overlap: seq 3 to 4 and seq 4 to 5 (a device that wrote again and also kept the earlier file). The reader sees seq 3, 4 and 5 once each.

vectors.name: folder/gather-small-segments
vectors.description: Alice's device wrote three single-record segments (seq 3, 4, 5) and then gathered them: one file 0000000003-0000000005.seg holds all three and the small ones are gone. The reader sees the same three records.

vectors.name: folder/leftover-tmp-file-is-ignored
vectors.description: A device crashed while writing: a file whose name begins with .tmp- holds record seq 4 (complete), beside the finished segment with seq 3. A reader ignores names beginning with .tmp-, so it reads seq 3 only (seq 4 is "behind", never an error).

vectors.name: folder/segment-complete
vectors.description: Two complete frames.

vectors.name: folder/segment-partial-length
vectors.description: A final frame with only two of its four length bytes: ignored.

vectors.name: folder/segment-length-only
vectors.description: A final frame with its length and none of its body: ignored.

vectors.name: folder/segment-short-body
vectors.description: A final frame with part of its body: ignored.

vectors.name: folder/segment-zero-length-frame
vectors.description: A zero-length frame is a complete (and useless) frame, not an incomplete one.

vectors.name: folder/segment-empty
vectors.description: An empty file.

vectors.name: folder/frame-length-exactly-largest-incomplete
vectors.description: A length of exactly 1,052,760 (the largest sealed record) with no body behind it: within the limit, so an incomplete final frame, ignored.

vectors.name: folder/frame-length-one-over-largest
vectors.description: A length of 1,052,761: longer than any sealed record, so reading stops here.

vectors.name: folder/frame-length-huge
vectors.description: A length of 4,294,967,295 (it would swallow the rest of the segment): reading stops.

vectors.name: folder/frame-length-exactly-largest-with-body
vectors.description: A length of 1,052,760 with that many bytes behind it: one frame (it is not a valid record, which is the reader's next check).

vectors.name: folder/segment-in-sequence
vectors.description: Three records of one chain in a segment, seq 1, 2, 3 (keys given so seq can be read).

vectors.name: folder/segment-gap-in-sequence
vectors.description: seq 1, then seq 3: out of sequence, reading stops after the first frame.

vectors.name: folder/segment-repeated-seq
vectors.description: seq 1 twice: out of sequence.

vectors.name: folder/segment-descending
vectors.description: seq 2 then seq 1: out of sequence.

vectors.name: folder/segment-starts-anywhere
vectors.description: A segment may begin at any seq (a covered range was deleted): seq 2 then 3 is in sequence.

vectors.name: folder/segment-frame-without-key-between-readable-frames
vectors.description: seq 2, 3, 4, 5 of one chain where the frame for seq 3 is sealed under a key the reader does not hold yet (epoch 1): that frame is kept and passed over, and the readable frames around it are still in sequence (seq 2 then seq 4 with one frame between them). All four frames are returned.

vectors.name: folder/segment-frame-without-key-then-a-gap
vectors.description: The same segment with the unreadable frame and then a readable frame that skips one seq (x1, unreadable, x4 = seq 2, 3, 5): out of sequence, reading stops before x4.

vectors.name: folder/segment-starts-with-a-frame-without-key
vectors.description: A segment that begins with an unreadable frame: nothing to compare it with, it is passed over, and the next readable frame is accepted wherever it starts.

vectors.name: folder/segment-unopenable-frame-passes
vectors.description: A frame the reader cannot open (no key for its group) has no known seq: it is passed through rather than stopping the segment (finding).
